recipes.name: Run 1
dims: Wedge (1/8 of a log), from a 12 in log
Length along the bark corner of the slanted sawn face

steps.title: Take the stock
steps.text: Take a wedge (1/8 of a log) stick at least 2.59 in long. Write 1 on it in chalk.

steps.title: Cut 1 (first end) on the mitre saw
steps.text: Lay the stick on the slanted sawn face on the saw table, with the bark corner of the slanted sawn face against the fence, the keeper to the LEFT of the blade. Mitre 35.3° — followed from the fence toward you, the cut drifts to the LEFT. Bevel 30.0° — top of the blade tilted to the LEFT. Slide it so the blade just clears the raw end everywhere -- about 0.5 in in from the end at its longest. The offcut, right of the blade, is a tapered piece: 4.53 in along the point, down to 0.50 in along the bark corner of the slanted sawn face. This cut meets the frame's 45° wall.

steps.title: Cut 2 (second end), marked and cut by hand
steps.text: Too steep for the mitre saw. Mark where this cut crosses each long corner, measured from the far end: 0.00 in along the point; 0.00 in along the bark corner of sawn 1; 0.00 in along the bark corner of the slanted sawn face. Join the marks on every face and cut to the lines with a circular saw, bandsaw or handsaw. The cut face has to lie on the frame's 45° wall: it leans 45.0° from the panel's plane.

steps.title: Cut 3 (second end), marked and cut by hand
steps.text: Too steep for the mitre saw. Mark where this cut crosses each long corner, measured from the far end: 70.91 in along the point; 79.22 in along the bark corner of sawn 1; 69.66 in along the bark corner of the slanted sawn face. Join the marks on every face and cut to the lines with a circular saw, bandsaw or handsaw. The cut face has to lie on the frame's 45° wall: it leans 45.0° from the panel's plane.

steps.title: Check it
steps.text: Finished: 1.84 in along the bark corner of the slanted sawn face. Measure each against the list before it goes in.

steps.title: Put it in
steps.text: It goes in as run 1: on a sawn face against the flat side, point toward the open run (like the frame).

Length along the bark corner of the slanted sawn face

steps.title: Take the stock
steps.text: Take a wedge (1/8 of a log) stick at least 8.28 in long. Write 13 on it in chalk.

steps.title: Cut 1 (first end) on the mitre saw
steps.text: Lay the stick on the slanted sawn face on the saw table, with the bark corner of the slanted sawn face against the fence, the keeper to the LEFT of the blade. Mitre 35.3° — followed from the fence toward you, the cut drifts to the LEFT. Bevel 30.0° — top of the blade tilted to the LEFT. Slide it so the blade just clears the raw end everywhere -- about 0.5 in in from the end at its longest. The offcut, right of the blade, is a tapered piece: 4.53 in along the point, down to 0.50 in along the bark corner of the slanted sawn face. This cut meets the frame's 45° wall.

steps.title: Cut 2 (second end), marked and cut by hand
steps.text: Too steep for the mitre saw. Mark where this cut crosses each long corner, measured from the far end: 76.98 in along the point; 68.66 in along the bark corner of sawn 1; 63.97 in along the bark corner of the slanted sawn face. Join the marks on every face and cut to the lines with a circular saw, bandsaw or handsaw. The cut face has to lie on the frame's 45° wall: it leans 45.0° from the panel's plane.

steps.title: Check it
steps.text: Finished: 7.53 in along the bark corner of the slanted sawn face. Measure each against the list before it goes in.

steps.title: Put it in
steps.text: It goes in as run 13: on a sawn face against the flat side, point toward the open run (like the frame).

steps: Stock: split 12 in logs into eighths with the chainsaw (0.25 in kerf).
Saw settings, held as the piece lies in the panel:
13 ends: mitre 0.0°, bevel 45.0° -- the 45° wall of the long edge
13 ends: mitre 55.6°, bevel 45.0° -- the 45° wall of the short edge
Cut each piece to its long length first, then make the end cuts; measure the short length on the flat-side face to check.
fitting: The first piece meets the 45° slope with its bark: it touches along one line, and leaves a wedge-shaped gap above it -- caulk it or pack it.
1 pieces near the corners are under 6 in long: cut them from offcuts.
Where a run meets a side wall at an angle, the end is a compound cut: the cut face has to lie on the 45° wall, so it is both mitred and bevelled.

prep.name: Stock: from log to wedges (1/8 log)

steps.title: Split the log in eighths
steps.text: Buck the 12 in log to the strut length. Halve it through the pith with the chainsaw (0.25 in kerf), quarter each half, then halve each quarter: eight wedges, each with two sawn faces 6.00 in wide meeting at the pith, bark 4.59 in across.

steps.title: Put it in

steps: Stock: split 12 in logs into eighths with the chainsaw (0.25 in kerf).
Saw settings, held as the piece lies in the panel:
13 ends: mitre 0.0°, bevel 45.0° -- the 45° wall of the long edge
13 ends: mitre 60.0°, bevel 45.0° -- the 45° wall of the long edge
Cut each piece to its long length first, then make the end cuts; measure the short length on the flat-side face to check.
fitting: The first piece meets the 45° slope with its bark: it touches along one line, and leaves a wedge-shaped gap above it -- caulk it or pack it.
1 pieces near the corners are under 6 in long: cut them from offcuts.
Where a run meets a side wall at an angle, the end is a compound cut: the cut face has to lie on the 45° wall, so it is both mitred and bevelled.

prep.name: Stock: from log to wedges (1/8 log)

steps.title: Split the log in eighths
steps.text: Buck the 12 in log to the strut length. Halve it through the pith with the chainsaw (0.25 in kerf), quarter each half, then halve each quarter: eight wedges, each with two sawn faces 6.00 in wide meeting at the pith, bark 4.59 in across.
